title: Umbra Loft after-dark concert series: neutralize six mixed-light live shots to the tonal wedge each carries, drive all six to one agent-built noir single-ink treatment, and data-merge a press-ready poster set
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com open call by a dark-aesthetic creative studio offering 'premium poster/banner/social creatives' and 'cinematic, color-graded' photo editing; the real posting names no client and attaches no images, so the brand is laundered to a FICTIONAL basement live-jazz venue, 'Umbra Loft', and the vague ask is fixed into a runnable, gradeable job. The venue is launching an autumn concert series and wants a cohesive noir gig-poster look built entirely from its own archive of six low-light performance photos shot on six different nights under mismatched club light. To make 'read as one matched set' checkable, a small neutral three-step tonal wedge (a black / mid-grey / white reference card) is clipped in one corner of every frame, so consistency becomes a measurable target rather than an eyeball claim. Pure connector-legal edit + authored-document build: the six supplied photos are corrected per-frame to the wedge, then transformed with an agent-authored single-ink noir treatment (desaturate to a neutral grayscale base -> a single-ink monochromatic tint, which is exactly image_apply_monochromatic_tint's documented 'make it duotone' use -> screened-poster halftone -> fine grain), then cropped and data-merged through the venue's own authored InDesign poster template into a press-ready series PDF (one act per page). NO generative fill / generative-expand / outpaint, NO text-to-image, NO upscaling, NO object-removal-with-reconstruction, NO split-tone gradient map, NO free-form placement. Numeric values (the single ink hex, halftone/grain, A2 poster and social sizes, wedge tolerance) are enrichment chosen to be concrete and gradeable.
one_line_ask: Take six archival low-light live-performance photos shot on different nights under mismatched club light (each carrying a neutral tonal reference wedge), correct each frame on its own terms to the wedge so the set shares one tonal footing, drive all six to a single signature noir gig-poster treatment held identical across the set, then deliver each as a print-ready A2 poster-ratio image and a square social tile and merge the set into the venue's authored poster template as a press-ready concert-series PDF.
full_brief: Umbra Loft, a basement live-jazz and spoken-word venue, is announcing its autumn after-dark concert series and wants one signature poster look built entirely from its own archive so every night in the series reads instantly as the same run. We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you six raw performance photos pulled from six different nights: a stand-up bassist under a single spot, a vocalist at a ribbon mic, a wide shot of the trio mid-set, a pianist's hands close in, a sax player caught in a hard spotlight, and the drummer at the back of the low stage. Here is the problem: they were shot handheld in near-dark on six different nights under whatever light the room had — warm house tungsten one night, a cold spill from the EXIT sign another, a hot spotlight that ran the highlights up, one frame that came out almost black, a muddy flat one, and one lit by a sickly green backstage tube — so straight out of the folder they are a mismatched jumble and a poster series made of mismatched frames looks cheap. To make this checkable we clipped a small neutral tonal reference wedge (a black, a mid-grey and a white patch side by side) into one corner of every shot. Your job, and the craft is here: bring the whole set to one shared tonal footing by correcting EACH frame on its own terms against the wedge it carries — the wedge's black patch must sit just off pure black, its mid patch must land on the same mid-grey across all six, and its white patch must stay just below clipping (no blown patch), with any color cast neutralized so the frame desaturates to a clean neutral grayscale. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch and do NOT auto-tone each frame to look fine on its own: the six did not start from the same place, so a single global move (or a per-frame auto that keys off each frame's own histogram) will leave some frames crushed, some washed and some muddy, and once the noir look is mapped over the top the mismatch is glaring. Each frame needs its own exposure, black/white-point and contrast decision to land on the shared wedge target; work out what is actually wrong with each frame and dial it its own correction. Tell us, per frame, the corrective move you applied so we can confirm the set was matched, not eyeballed. Second, the look itself is yours to build and hold identical across all six: a deep, moody noir gig-poster treatment — the frame driven to a neutral grayscale base and carried into a single signature ink so it reads as one screened poster run, with a subtle print-screen halftone texture so it feels silk-screened and fine grain so the flat ink does not band on a large print, edges falling dark so the performer reads as hero. It must be the SAME treatment on every frame; there is no loadable preset to lean on, only our one-page look target (neutral wedge footing + the single poster ink + screened texture + dark falloff), so you are building the look from primitive tone controls and holding it constant, not picking a filter. Third, build the series: we have hand-built the InDesign poster template with the real placeholder fields (series name, act, night, set time) and an image slot for the treated poster, and we are giving you the running order — merge them so every night in the series gets its own poster page with its copy bound and its matching treated frame dropped in, then hand back one press-ready A2 poster PDF covering the whole series (one page per night). Deliver, per photo, a print-ready A2 poster-ratio image and a 1:1 social tile, plus the merged series PDF. The wedge is a working reference only — it must be cropped out of the finished poster and tile; keep it in frame on the graded masters you hand back so we can confirm the match, but it must not appear on any delivered poster.

inputs.name: set_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld phone-and-camera snapshot of a stand-up double-bass player performing under a single warm tungsten stage spot in a dim basement jazz club, near-dark room, distinctly WARM/amber cast and slightly UNDER-exposed and flat, the frame tilted about 3 degrees, cluttered dark background of cabling, an amp and a monitor wedge with a few blurred audience heads. Clipped to the monitor wedge in the lower corner of the frame, a small neutral three-step tonal reference card showing a black patch, a mid-grey patch and a white patch side by side, no color tint on the card itself. Real skin texture, wood grain on the bass, natural highlight on the strings, candid documentary concert feel, motion blur on the plucking hand, portrait orientation roughly 4000x6000 px shot on a real full-frame mirrorless at high ISO, never CGI-glossy.
inputs.realism_notes: Frame 1 of the series and one of the two TILTED frames (needs image_auto_straighten before anything else; leveling is a per-frame judgement, not every frame is tilted). Deliberately WARM + under + flat so its corrective move (lift exposure, cool the warm cast to neutral, seat the wedge's black/mid/white on the shared target) is real work and DIFFERENT from the other frames. The in-frame tonal wedge is the ground truth the agent corrects to by eye. Portrait ~4000x6000 camera-scale so the A2 poster crop (2896x4096) is a downscale, never an upscale, and the corner wedge falls outside the poster crop while staying in the retained master.

inputs.name: set_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld snapshot of a jazz vocalist leaning into a vintage ribbon microphone on a small stage, eyes closed mid-phrase, dim club light with a single warm key on one side and a cold blue-green spill from an EXIT sign on the other so the cast is split and mixed, level frame, normal exposure, distracting background of a drum kit, cymbals catching stray light and a cluttered merch shelf. Propped at the lower frame edge, the same small neutral three-step tonal reference card (black / mid-grey / white patches). Real skin pores, flyaway hair, sweat sheen, natural catchlight in the eye, candid documentary feel, portrait orientation roughly 4000x6000 px, real full-frame capture at high ISO, no studio gloss, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Frame 2, LEVEL (no straighten). Split warm-key / cold-EXIT cast: the hardest to neutralize, the agent must balance temperature and tint to a compromise that lands the wedge neutral rather than fully killing one side, then seat the wedge tonal target. A different correction axis and magnitude from frame 1 — copying frame 1's numbers here leaves it mismatched.

inputs.name: set_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal wide handheld snapshot of a three-piece jazz trio mid-set on a low basement stage (double bass, piano, drums), dim house wash, MUDDY and flat with low contrast and a faint warm haze, level frame, busy background of exposed brick, cabling taped to the floor, a PA speaker and the backs of a few audience heads in the foreground. In one corner, the same small neutral three-step tonal reference card (black / mid-grey / white patches). Real instrument texture, natural stage-light falloff, candid concert-documentary realism, slight high-ISO grain, portrait orientation roughly 4000x6000 px, real full-frame capture, never CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Frame 3, LEVEL. The muddy / low-contrast member: the dominant corrective is contrast + clarity to defeat the haze and pull the wedge's three patches apart to the shared target, with only a faint warm trim — a tonal problem, not a white-balance problem, so a WB-only pass fails here. Distinct move again.

inputs.name: set_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal tight handheld snapshot of a pianist's hands on the keys under a low warm lamp in a dark basement club, strongly UNDER-exposed and nearly black with only the keys and knuckles catching light, warm cast, level frame, dark cluttered background of the piano lid and a cabled mic. Sitting on the piano lid in the corner of the frame, the same small neutral three-step tonal reference card (black / mid-grey / white patches), sitting dark. Real skin texture on the hands, wood and key detail, candid documentary feel, portrait orientation roughly 4000x6000 px, real full-frame capture at very high ISO, never CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Frame 4, LEVEL. The exposure-rescue member: a large exposure + shadow lift of UNIQUE magnitude is needed to bring the wedge up to legibility and the mid patch onto the shared target, held in check so the white patch does not blow and the black patch stays off pure black. Copying any other frame's exposure here visibly under- or over-shoots — the magnitude is specific to this frame.

inputs.name: set_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld snapshot of a saxophone player caught in a hard bright spotlight on a basement stage, the highlights on the brass and the player's forehead riding near clipping, OVER-exposed and hot with a warm cast, level frame, dark surrounding room with a monitor and cabling. In the lower corner, the same small neutral three-step tonal reference card (black / mid-grey / white patches), its white patch near blown. Real brass reflection, skin sheen, candid documentary concert feel, portrait orientation roughly 4000x6000 px, real full-frame capture, never CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Frame 5, LEVEL. The OVER-exposed member and the tonal OPPOSITE of frame 4: the corrective must pull exposure / highlights / whites DOWN off the clip so the wedge's white patch recovers below clipping while the black patch and mid land on the shared target, plus a slight cool toward neutral. Applying frame 4's big lift here blows it out entirely — the batch genuinely needs opposite-direction moves.

inputs.name: set_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal handheld snapshot of a drummer mid-set at the back of a low basement stage, lit by a sickly GREEN backstage fluorescent tube spill, distinct green cast, the frame tilted about 4 degrees, normal-to-flat exposure, busy dark background of cymbals, a brick wall and taped cabling. Gaffer-taped to a cymbal stand in the corner, the same small neutral three-step tonal reference card (black / mid-grey / white patches), visibly skewing green. Real drum hardware texture, natural stage-light falloff, candid documentary feel, portrait orientation roughly 4000x6000 px, real full-frame capture at high ISO, never CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Frame 6 and the second TILTED frame (needs image_auto_straighten). The green fluorescent cast is on the TINT axis, not the temperature axis — a warm/cool move can never clear it; the correct neutralization pushes tint toward MAGENTA so the wedge reads neutral and desaturates clean, then seats the wedge tonal target. This is the frame that most cleanly exposes a one-global-WB or temperature-only or per-frame-auto-tone approach, because none of those touch a green cast — its wedge would stay green and its grayscale would carry a residual dirty value while the others look fixed.

inputs.name: umbra_look_target.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED one-page look-target sheet (supplied by the venue, NOT model-generated and NOT a loadable develop preset): states the Umbra Loft after-dark poster look in words and reference swatches only — every treated frame is driven to a neutral grayscale base with the in-frame tonal wedge on a shared footing (black just off pure black, mid at a consistent mid-grey across the set, white just below clipping), then carried into ONE single signature poster ink (a deep near-black cool ink, hex #14161F) as a monochromatic tint across the whole frame, with a subtle print-screen halftone texture, fine grain, and edges falling dark so the performer reads as hero. One line: 'Every night in the series must carry the identical treatment so the run reads as one set; keep it deep and moody, edges to near-black.' It is a target to hit by building the look from primitive tone controls, not a preset to apply.
inputs.realism_notes: Deliberately a written/visual TARGET, not an .xmp or a built-in preset name — the connector cannot load a custom develop preset, so the noir look must be reproduced with authored adjustments and a single-ink monochromatic tint and held identical across the set. Supplies ONE poster ink (the monochromatic-tint color) and the tonal footing; it does NOT specify a two-ink amber/ink split-tone, because a controlled split-tone gradient map is not connector-doable — the deliverable is a genuine single-ink monotone, which is exactly image_apply_monochromatic_tint's documented duotone use. The numeric wedge tolerance belongs to the grader, not to any step the agent performs.

inputs.name: umbra_poster_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A2 portrait (420x594mm) concert-series poster — ONE act per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<series>>, <<act>>, <<night>> and <<set_time>> set in the venue's poster type, plus ONE @-prefixed image-path merge column @image wired to a full-bleed A2 image frame that holds the treated poster art. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the treated poster reaches the page ONLY as a merge bind through this image frame; the type is set by the template, not drawn by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and the image field actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (that would not bind fields) and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one page per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus a genuine @image-path column, and it produces ONE PAGE PER ROW, so a single-record A2 poster is the correct connector-doable shape and N nights -> an N-page series PDF. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. The @image column binds the AGENT'S OWN treated poster art (named per the running order the agent assigns), so the deliverable's distinctive quality — the noir treatment — is the agent's, dropped onto the venue's template.

inputs.name: umbra_series_runorder.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns series,act,night,set_time,@image holding six rows, one per night of the autumn after-dark series. series is the same fictional series name on every row (e.g. 'Umbra After-Dark Sessions'); act is a distinct fictional act/performer name per row (all coined, e.g. 'The Marlow Vane Trio', 'Cass Ondine', 'The Halloway Set', 'Delphine Roux Quartet', 'Sable and the Nightporters', 'Idris Cole'); night is a date/day per row; set_time is a start time (e.g. '9:30 PM'). The @image column names the treated poster art the agent produces for that night (e.g. @poster_01.jpg .. @poster_06.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each treated A2 frame into that night's single-record poster page. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<series>>,<<act>>,<<night>>,<<set_time>> and the @image-path column @image.
inputs.realism_notes: Six rows -> the merge must produce exactly six poster pages (page-count = row-count is a checkable gate). All copy is bound VERBATIM from this CSV — no rewriting. The @image column carries the AGENT-PRODUCED treated poster filenames the agent assigns per running order; every frame gets the identical noir treatment, so nothing in this file telegraphs any per-frame diagnosis or treatment — it is running-order and copy only. Coined act names, no real performer, band, label, festival or trademark.

outputs.name: umbra_graded_masters_x6
outputs.spec: The six fully-treated card-BEARING masters (the pre-crop full-res ~4000x6000 frames, tonal wedge still in frame), RETAINED so the harness can grade the match. Each was corrected on its own terms to its in-frame wedge and then carried through the identical agent-authored noir treatment (neutral grayscale base -> single-ink monochromatic tint #14161F -> subtle halftone -> fine grain -> dark edge falloff). Acceptance (grader-checked, measured on these retained masters, never on a card-removed crop): on every frame the wedge's three patches read as a consistent monotone ramp landing on the shared footing — the black patch just off pure black, the mid patch at a common mid-grey (within ~4 levels across the set), the white patch just below clipping — so the six read as one screened poster run; and the noir ink/halftone/grain look is visibly identical across all six. Accompanied by the per-frame corrective-move report.

outputs.name: umbra_posters_a2_x6
outputs.spec: Six print-ready A2 poster-ratio images (1:1.414 portrait, 2896x4096 px, ~175 DPI at A2, print-review resolution), one per performance frame, each the identical noir single-ink treatment, cropped to the A2 poster ratio with the tonal wedge cropped OUT (no card pixels present). These are the frames that bind into the series merge. Acceptance (grader-checked): card-exclusion is verified HERE (no wedge in frame); the tonal-match tolerance is never evaluated on these crops — it is evaluated on the retained card-bearing masters.

outputs.name: umbra_social_tiles_x6
outputs.spec: Six 1:1 (1080x1080) social tiles of the same six treated frames, matched to the poster treatment, cropped square with the performer centred and the tonal wedge cropped OUT, so the run still reads as one noir series at thumbnail size.

outputs.name: umbra_series_posters.pdf
outputs.spec: One press-ready A2 concert-series poster PDF exported from the one-page-per-row InDesign data-merge: exactly six pages (page-count = row-count = 6), each binding that night's series/act/night/set_time copy verbatim from the run-order CSV into the authored template's live <<fields>> with its matching treated A2 poster dropped into the full-bleed image frame via @image (a merge bind, never free-form placement); ~175 DPI print-review. Acceptance (grader-checked): six pages, each carrying a distinct act's copy over its treated frame, all sharing the identical noir look. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged document in one call — no per-record named export.

outputs.name: grade_params_report
outputs.spec: A short written report the agent authors and returns listing, per frame (set_01..set_06), the final corrective move it APPLIED to reach the wedge target — the exposure delta, the black/white-point and contrast moves, and the white-balance direction (cool the warm frames, warm the cool frames, push tint toward magenta on the green frame, exposure-rescue the near-black frame, recover the over-exposed frame) — plus a one-line confirmation of the shared noir look parameters (the single ink, halftone and grain) applied identically to all six. This is an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement: the agent knows these values because it set them by eye. Acceptance (grader-checked): the six reported corrections are NON-identical and their directions match each frame's stated problem — in particular the green frame carries a tint (not a temperature) move and the under- and over-exposed frames move in opposite exposure directions — while the noir look parameters are identical across the set.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: set_01.jpg, set_02.jpg, set_03.jpg, set_04.jpg, set_05.jpg, set_06.jpg, umbra_look_target.pdf, umbra_poster_template.indd, umbra_series_runorder.csv
connector_workflow.note: Ingest the six raw performance photos, the one-page look target, the authored poster template and the run-order CSV so every downstream edit and the merge run against real asset references. Plumbing only — not part of the difficulty.

Frame 1 is tilted ~3 deg — level it first (image_auto_straighten is the ONLY tool that rectifies a tilt). Deciding WHICH frames are tilted is part of the job: only frames 1 and 6 get this; the level frames skip it.

Frame 1 (warm, under, flat): judge the in-frame wedge by eye and COOL the warm cast to neutral, LIFT exposure out of the flat under-exposure, and set black/white points so the wedge's black patch sits just off pure black, its mid patch lands on the shared mid-grey and its white patch stays below clipping. Reason these to THIS frame's problem; do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / image_adjust_brightness_and_contrast / image_adjust_vibrance_and_saturation the prior spec used).

Apply the SHARED authored noir look, part 1, held identical for all six: fully desaturate to a neutral grayscale base (saturation to -100, killing the now-neutralized cast) and lay in the fixed noir tonal shape — a hard contrast S-curve and clarity that pulls the lit performer off the dark room and drops the edges toward near-black. This tonal SHAPE is a batch constant (unlike the per-frame correction in step 3); building it from primitives is what makes the look agent-authored, not a preset and not auto_tone.

Apply the SHARED single poster ink identically: a whole-image monochromatic tint in the deep near-black cool ink #14161F from the look target. This is the connector-legal noir 'duotone' — image_apply_monochromatic_tint's own documented 'make it duotone' use, a single ink mapped across the grayscale ramp. NOT a two-ink split-tone: image_apply_color_overlay (whole-image, no opacity, no blend control) would just flood the entire frame flat and image_apply_fill_area is a solid dead-fill — both destroy the tonal ramp, so neither can build a second highlight ink, and neither is used.
Apply the SHARED subtle print-screen halftone dot texture (small radius) identically so the treatment reads as a silk-screened gig poster.

Add the SHARED fine film grain identically so the flat single ink does not band on large-format A2 print. s01_master is the card-BEARING treated master (tonal wedge still in frame) RETAINED as a grading artifact — the wedge match is graded HERE, never on the cropped poster.

Crop the treated master to the A2 portrait poster ratio at 2896x4096 (~175 DPI at A2), framing on the performer with the corner tonal wedge cropped OUT — this card-removed poster is what binds into the series merge. Downscale-only from the ~4000x6000 source, never canvas-extend, never upscale.
Crop the same treated master to a 1:1 1080x1080 social tile, performer centred, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.

Frame 2 is LEVEL (no straighten). Split warm-key / cold-EXIT cast: balance temperature AND tint to a compromise that drives the wedge neutral (accepting one side stays slightly warmer) rather than fully killing one side, then seat the wedge's black/mid/white on the shared target. A different axis and magnitude from frame 1. Report the move.
Shared noir look part 1 (identical to step 4): desaturate to the neutral grayscale base and lay in the same fixed contrast S-curve + clarity + dark falloff.
Shared single-ink monochromatic tint #14161F (identical to step 5).
Shared halftone (identical to step 6).
Shared grain (identical to step 7). s02_master is the retained card-bearing treated master for frame 2.
A2 poster crop of frame 2, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.
1:1 1080x1080 social tile of frame 2, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.

Frame 3 is LEVEL. Muddy / low-contrast / faint-warm: the dominant move is a strong contrast + clarity recovery to defeat the haze and pull the wedge's three patches apart onto the shared target, plus a small warm trim toward neutral — a tonal problem, not a WB one. Land the mid patch without crushing the black patch or blowing the white. Report the contrast/clarity and warm applied.
Shared noir look part 1 (identical to step 4).
Shared single-ink monochromatic tint #14161F (identical to step 5).
Shared halftone (identical to step 6).
Shared grain (identical to step 7). s03_master retained as frame 3's card-bearing master.
A2 poster crop of frame 3, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.
1:1 social tile of frame 3, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.

Frame 4 is LEVEL. The exposure-rescue frame: a LARGE exposure + shadow lift of magnitude unique to this near-black frame to bring the wedge up to legibility and the mid patch onto the shared target, held by pulling highlights/whites so the recovered frame does not blow the white patch and the black patch stays off pure black, plus a slight cool of the warm lamp. Copying any other frame's exposure here under- or over-shoots. Report the exposure/shadow/highlight moves.
Shared noir look part 1 (identical to step 4).
Shared single-ink monochromatic tint #14161F (identical to step 5).
Shared halftone (identical to step 6).
Shared grain (identical to step 7). s04_master retained as frame 4's card-bearing master.
A2 poster crop of frame 4, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.
1:1 social tile of frame 4, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.

Frame 5 is LEVEL. The over-exposed frame and the tonal OPPOSITE of frame 4: pull exposure / highlights / whites DOWN off the clip so the wedge's white patch recovers below clipping, seat the black and mid on the shared target, and cool the warm cast slightly. Applying frame 4's lift here destroys it — proving the batch needs opposite-direction moves, not one recipe. Report the recovery moves.
Shared noir look part 1 (identical to step 4).
Shared single-ink monochromatic tint #14161F (identical to step 5).
Shared halftone (identical to step 6).
Shared grain (identical to step 7). s05_master retained as frame 5's card-bearing master.
A2 poster crop of frame 5, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.
1:1 social tile of frame 5, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only.
Frame 6 is tilted ~4 deg — level it (the second and last tilted frame).

Frame 6: green fluorescent cast — a TINT-axis problem. Push tint toward MAGENTA (with only a small temperature trim) so the wedge reads neutral and the frame desaturates to a CLEAN neutral grayscale, then seat the wedge's black/mid/white on the shared target. A temperature-only move, a single global WB copied from the warm/cool frames, or a per-frame auto-tone cannot clear a green cast at all — the wedge would stay green and carry a dirty residual value into the grayscale, the visible failure this frame catches. Report the magenta tint and confirm it is a tint (not a temperature) move.
Shared noir look part 1 (identical to step 4).
Shared single-ink monochromatic tint #14161F (identical to step 5).
Shared halftone (identical to step 6).
Shared grain (identical to step 7). s06_master retained as frame 6's card-bearing master; s01_master..s06_master together form umbra_graded_masters_x6.
A2 poster crop of frame 6, wedge cropped OUT. Downscale-only. poster_01.jpg..poster_06.jpg form umbra_posters_a2_x6 and are the frames the merge binds.
1:1 social tile of frame 6, wedge cropped OUT. tile_01.jpg..tile_06.jpg form umbra_social_tiles_x6.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: poster_01.jpg, poster_02.jpg, poster_03.jpg, poster_04.jpg, poster_05.jpg, poster_06.jpg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the six treated A2 posters so the merge can resolve them by the run-order CSV's @image column. Files uploaded under the exact names the CSV references (poster_01.jpg .. poster_06.jpg). Plumbing.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the CSV's @image column resolves to for each night's poster page. Plumbing.

One-page-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the six run-order rows (series/act/night/set_time) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD A2 .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve the @image column per row — drop that night's treated poster into the full-bleed image frame — producing EXACTLY ONE poster page per row (six pages). The treated art reaches the page ONLY as this merge bind; free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned. [T] requires the hand-authored template with its merge-wired image frame; a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind and a multi-record grid is impossible.

Export the merged single-record poster pages to a press-ready ~175 DPI A2 PDF, one page per night. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all six posters) in a single call — it cannot pull one named page out on its own, so there is no per-record export. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 6; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chaining throughout. All nine assets enter once via asset_add_file(1). Each of the six frames runs a per-frame sub-chain that splits into a DIVERGENT correction stage and a SHARED look stage: image_apply_adjustments neutralizes THAT frame's specific problem to its in-frame tonal wedge (the WB/exposure/contrast inputs differ per frame), then a fixed four-step noir look is applied identically — image_apply_adjustments (desaturate + shared contrast S-curve/clarity/dark-falloff) -> image_apply_monochromatic_tint (the single ink #14161F) -> image_apply_halftone -> image_add_grain — producing the card-bearing treated master, which is then cropped two ways (A2 poster with the wedge OUT, 1:1 social tile with the wedge OUT). image_auto_straighten is inserted only on the two TILTED frames (1 and 6) before their correction. Sub-chains: frame 1 = steps 2-9, frame 2 = 10-15, frame 3 = 16-22, frame 4 = 23-29, frame 5 = 30-36, frame 6 = 37-44 (frame 6's correction pulls from its straightened output s06_level).
